## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

content.text:
The project is empty. Need to build a 3D Truck Simulator like Euro Truck Simulator 2 — a complete playable game. Tech: Three.js with Vite, probably. Need to check whether npm install works (network). Let's plan a substantial game:

Features:
- 3D open world with roads, terrain, towns, hills, trees
- A truck (semi tractor + trailer) with physics-ish driving, gears, engine sound
- Camera modes (chase, hood, cockpit...)
- Delivery jobs: pick cargo, drive to destination, damage, time
- HUD: speed, gear, fuel, money, minimap, GPS route
- Day/night, weather, traffic cars
- Mobile touch controls/responsive
- Menu start screen, pause, settings (audio, graphics quality)
- Save game via localStorage
- Map with waypoints, route guidance arrow
- Fuel stations, repair? Maybe simple.
- Economy: money, XP/level, upgrades? Simplified: jobs, payment based on distance and cargo, damage penalty, fuel cost.

Given time, build a solid single-page game with Three.js. Use Vite. Need to verify install network. Let's try `npm install three vite` quickly.

Design specifics:
- Terrain: procedural heightmap around a road network? ETS2-like highways. Simpler: flat terrain with rolling hills, a set of straight road segments connecting cities in a loop (polyline circuit), plus intersections. Use road spline points defining a circuit with cities along the way.
- Build road geometry from centerline spline using CatmullRom closed curve: generate ribbon mesh with shoulders, dashed lane markings. Terrain height adjusted to sample near road. Simpler: roads flat at y=0 on a largely flat plane with distant hills mesh for scenery. To look good, add gentle terrain undulation far from road.

For playability: Circuit road loop ~ several km with towns, checkpoints. Jobs: start at depot, destination city some distance along loop. GPS arrow, route line on minimap. Deliver within timer. Cargo load visuals (trailer included always).

Truck: build from boxes/cylinders with nice materials — cab with windshield, chrome grill, lights, wheels with rotation and steering, trailer with cargo box. Physics: arcade bicycle model with acceleration, drag, braking, gearbox automatic/sequential, reverse, steering. Collision: keep truck close to road? Off-road slows and adds damage. Simple collision with traffic cars; traffic follows road lanes.

Environment: sky gradient shader, sun, fog, clouds? Trees along road, mountains, buildings in towns, guardrails, street lights, signs. Day-night with headlights, lamp posts.

Audio: WebAudio engine hum synthesized with oscillators, gear shift, horn, UI clicks, rain? Include mute toggle.

Mobile: touch steering buttons / accelerator. Detect touch. Responsive HUD. Use WebGL (three) not WebGPU for reliability in SwiftShader.

Performance: use InstancedMesh for trees, guardrails posts, buildings maybe. Keep draw calls low. Shadows on maybe low-res; allow quality toggle.

Game flow:
- Main menu styled like ETS2: title "TRANS EUROPA", Start, Continue (save), Settings.
- Job selection screen: cards with cargo/from/to/distance/reward. Accept -> game start at depot.
- While driving: HUD speedometer, tacho, gear, fuel, damage, route progress, minimap, delivery info, time remaining.
- Reach destination marker -> park in zone (speed < ~5) -> delivery complete screen with payout breakdown, then choose next job.
- Fuel: fuel drains, gas station zones to refill (drive slow inside), costs money.
- Damage increases when off-road or collisions. Repair at service? Maybe simplify.
- XP/level with money.
- Pause menu (Esc), settings for quality and volume, reset save.
- Minimap with roads, cities, truck marker, destination.
- Photo mode? Not necessary.

Implementation files:
- index.html
- src/main.js (game loop)
- src/world.js (terrain, road spline, props)
- src/truck.js
- src/traffic.js
- src/audio.js
- src/hud.js? Could be single CSS + JS modules. Keep manageable but organized: main.js, world.js, truck.js, traffic.js, audio.js, ui.js, jobs.js.
- style.css
- vite.config.js maybe not needed; use npm scripts "dev": "vite --port 3002". Note start.sh uses runtime default-start.mjs; likely it detects vite? Let me check runtime scripts to know how serving works.

Let's inspect RUNTIME_DIR scripts.

It auto-clicks a start button if found (CAPTURE_AUTO_START default true). Our menu needs a start button; screenshot will show game? It clicks button matching selector heuristics. Let's check capture-start.mjs / wip-screenshots.cjs to understand auto-start.

Auto-start clicks a button whose label exactly "start"/"start game"/"play"/"play now". Our menu can have "Start Game" button that goes to job selection. Screenshot then job screen. For our own checks, we can use playwright-cli manually to play.

Let's set up Vite + three. Check network install.
